answer.rationale: With the line at 94% of committed volume and no buffer, any switch or dual-sourcing introduces onboarding/integration risk during a 14-day window that the plant cannot absorb (contra memory_c2's switching case, which was a different market/component and doesn't establish current-vendor equivalence). Renewing without changes doesn't address the mandated 18% spend cut. Deferring isn't viable since this is the primary, capacity-critical contract, not the non-critical one in memory_c5. Negotiating terms at renewal (memory_c4) and pursuing a longer commitment for volume pricing (memory_c6) both directly target cost reduction while preserving the existing qualified supply chain and delivery continuity (memory_c1), aligning with minimizing TCO without raising delivery risk. I verified c4 and c6 because they are the load-bearing memories for this specific action and its cost-savings claim; the others are lower-stakes context I'm treating as directionally reliable rather than confirmed.
